title: JADE-B evaluates genetic-cholestasis risk in infants
summary: Random-forest JADE-B used routine early clinical features to evaluate genetic causes of infant cholestasis. Development used 1,008 infants, and an external retrospective 98-case cohort from Thailand and Korea yielded an AUC of 0.7115. Estimates of potentially avoided genetic tests were modeled rather than observed clinical savings. Prospective referral safety and broader diagnostic utility remain untested.

source_review.scope: Primary full paper relevant model Methods, study Results and limitations; exact primary front-matter identity and Europe PMC metadata checked.

evidence.tested: Internal split and external retrospective 98-case genetic-diagnosis validation.
evidence.unknown: Prospective resource allocation, safe testing deferral and treatment benefit remain unestablished.
evidence.ai_role: Random forest learns genetic-disease classification from 20 accessible features available within one month of disease presentation.
